clinical_knowledge.topic: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Order staging baseline PET-CT scan from neck to pelvis and echocardiogram/PFTs (before chemotherapy), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: painless neck lumps, drenching night sweats, and 15-pound weight loss over 3 months

Key HPI features: 24F presents with 3-month history of painless, rubbery swelling on the right side of her neck and above her collarbone. Reports drenching night sweats requiring her to change pajamas every night, unexplained low-grade fevers, and 15-pound weight loss. Also notes severe itching after drinking wine.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 37.9C, HR 88. 3 cm firm, rubbery, nontender right cervical and 2 cm right supraclavicular lymph nodes palpable. No splenomegaly. Bloods: FBC shows mild normocytic anemia, ESR 68 mm/hr, LDH elevated at 340 U/L. Excisional lymph node biopsy reveals Reed-Sternberg cells (binucleated 'owl-eye' appearance, CD15+, CD30+) within a collagen-banded background.
Relevant background/PMH: Treated for presumed lymphadenitis by GP with amoxicillin 1 month ago without effect
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Non-Hodgkin lymphoma without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) — signal more advanced disease.
management_principles: Order staging baseline PET-CT scan from neck to pelvis and echocardiogram/PFTs (before chemotherapy)
Refer to medical oncology for initiation of ABVD chemotherapy regimen (Doxorubicin, Bleomycin, Vinblastine, Dacarbazine)
Offer fertility preservation counseling prior to treatment
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 24F presenting with classic 'B symptoms' (night sweats, fever, weight loss), alcohol-induced pruritus, and painless cervical/supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 37.9C, HR 88. 3 cm firm, rubbery, nontender right cervical and 2 cm right supraclavicular lymph nodes palpable. No splenomegaly. Bloods: FBC shows mild normocytic anemia, ESR 68 mm/hr, LDH elevated at 340 U/L. Excisional lymph node biopsy reveals Reed-Sternberg cells (binucleated 'owl-eye' appearance, CD15+, CD30+) within a collagen-banded background.
reference_soap.assessment: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype, clinical stage IIB (pending PET-CT).
reference_soap.plan: Order staging baseline PET-CT scan from neck to pelvis and echocardiogram/PFTs (before chemotherapy). Refer to medical oncology for initiation of ABVD chemotherapy regimen (Doxorubicin, Bleomycin, Vinblastine, Dacarbazine). Offer fertility preservation counseling prior to treatment.

learning_objectives: Correlate classic 'B symptoms' and painless lymphadenopathy with Hodgkin/Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
Identify Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15+, CD30+) on excisional lymph node biopsy
Outline systematic staging protocol including PET-CT and baseline cardiopulmonary toxicity screens
Counsel young adult oncology patients on oncofertility preservation options prior to chemotherapy

teaching.one_liner: A lymph node cancer marked by painless, rubbery lymphadenopathy, drenching night sweats, weight loss, and — classically — itching triggered by alcohol.
red_flags: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) — signal more advanced disease

must_ask.say: Is the lump painless and rubbery, and has it been growing?
Have you had night sweats heavy enough to soak your clothes, fevers, or weight loss?
Does the area itch or hurt after drinking alcohol?
How many months has the lump been there?
Did antibiotics from your doctor make any difference?
